subject: Physics
source: Paraphrased exemplars in the style of Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Physics 1PH0 Papers 1 and 2 (2018 onwards). Stems are author-original; mark allocations follow Edexcel mark scheme conventions.

exemplars.stem: A car travels 240 m in 16 s. Calculate the average speed of the car.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for v = s/t. A1 for 15 m/s.

exemplars.stem: A force of 24 N acts on a trolley of mass 6 kg. Calculate the acceleration of the trolley, ignoring friction.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for F = ma rearranged to a = F/m. M1 for 24/6. A1 for 4 m/s².
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Core Practical style — Newton's second law

exemplars.stem: A trolley of mass 0.80 kg moves at 3.0 m/s and collides with a stationary trolley of mass 1.20 kg. After the collision the two trolleys move together. Calculate the speed of the combined trolleys after the collision.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for momentum before = 0.80 × 3.0 = 2.4 kg m/s. M1 for momentum after = (0.80 + 1.20) × v. M1 for 2.4 = 2.0 v. A1 for 1.2 m/s.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Paper 2H style — momentum conservation (HT reasoning)

exemplars.stem: A weightlifter raises a 60 kg mass through a vertical height of 2.0 m in 1.5 s. Calculate the work done against gravity, taking g = 10 N/kg.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for weight = mg = 60 × 10 = 600 N. M1 for W = Fd = 600 × 2.0. A1 for 1200 J.

exemplars.stem: A wave on the surface of water has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 0.40 m. Calculate the speed of the wave.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for v = fλ. M1 for 5 × 0.40. A1 for 2.0 m/s.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Core Practical style — wave equation

exemplars.stem: State one use and one danger of microwaves and one use and one danger of ultraviolet radiation from the electromagnetic spectrum.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: microwaves — use (e.g. communications, cooking) and danger (heating internal tissues). 1 mark: UV — use (e.g. tanning, fluorescent tubes, vitamin D) and danger (skin cancer, eye damage). Reward any 3 valid points across both bands.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Paper 2F style — EM spectrum uses and dangers

exemplars.stem: A radioactive sample has an initial count rate of 640 counts per minute. After 8 days the count rate is 80 counts per minute. Calculate the half-life of the sample.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for 640 → 320 → 160 → 80 = 3 half-lives. M1 for 8 days / 3 half-lives. A1 for 8/3 ≈ 2.67 days.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Paper 2 style — half-life from count rate

exemplars.stem: Explain how observations of light from distant galaxies provide evidence for the Big Bang theory of the universe.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: light from distant galaxies is shifted towards the red end of the spectrum. 1 mark: this red shift is greater for galaxies further away. 1 mark: this shows the galaxies are moving away from us / universe is expanding. 1 mark: an expanding universe is consistent with the Big Bang origin (everything started from a single point and expanded outwards).
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1PH0 Paper 2H style — red shift evidence (HT reasoning)
